claude.sample_unit: simulated patients plus emergency department encounters (count not reported in abstract)

links.outcome: PPV, sensitivity, mean rank of true positives when ranking by predicted risk versus risk groups under resource constraints
links.effect: Ranking patients by predicted probabilities gave better performance than risk groups alone; benefits grew with discrimination and prevalence and were greatest when resource constraints were highest.
links.quote: Using predicted probabilities to rank patients by predicted risk led to model performance benefits when compared to risk groups alone.

unlisted_practices: Retain and share continuous predicted risk scores rather than dichotomizing into risk groups, using them with clinical judgment for prioritization within risk groups

links.effect: Predicted-probability ranking improved PPV, sensitivity, and mean rank versus risk groups alone; no numerical effect sizes reported.
